denotes those to whom one becomes dear

items.question: What attainment makes a practitioner dear to the yoginīs?
premises: Enjoyment and liberation can be attained together
Great accomplishment arises as a result
Such accomplishment brings favor with the yoginīs
items.inference: One who attains great accomplishment in enjoyment and liberation becomes dear to the yoginīs
items.plain_english: He may attain the great accomplishment of enjoyment and liberation and become dear to the yoginīs.

items.question: Which chapter concludes in the setting of Candra-dvīpa?
premises: The text marks a chapter conclusion
The setting is identified as Candra-dvīpa
The chapter is numbered as the ninth
items.inference: The ninth chapter concludes in Candra-dvīpa
items.plain_english: Thus ends the ninth chapter, which emerged in Candra-dvīpa.

rows.grounds: describes the posture of the self

items.question: In what posture is the self visualized when surrounded by fire?
premises: The self is imagined as surrounded by fire
The posture involves standing
The stance is on one foot
items.inference: The self is visualized standing on one foot surrounded by fire
items.plain_english: Visualize the self surrounded by fire, standing on one foot.

rows.grounds: specifies what is to be determined

items.question: What revelation about knowledge is requested from the deity now?
premises: The speaker addresses the deity directly
The speaker asks for a determination of knowledge
The request is for it to be made manifest now
items.inference: The speaker asks the deity to reveal the determination of knowledge now
items.plain_english: O God, make manifest to me now the determination of knowledge.

rows.grounds: second member indicating groups of eight

items.question: What division of eightfold groups is sought to be known exhaustively?
premises: The subject concerns divisions into octads
There are eight such octads
The aim is to know this division fully and endlessly
items.inference: The speaker seeks exhaustive knowledge of the division into eight octads
uncertainties: anantathā may indicate infinite extent or thoroughness
items.plain_english: I wish to know fully and endlessly the division into eight octads.

items.question: How does the secret place function as a wheel for swift accomplishment?
premises: A secret place is identified as a wheel
The wheel is associated with accomplishment
The accomplishment occurs quickly
items.inference: The secret place, as a wheel, brings about swift accomplishment
items.plain_english: O Bhairava, tell how the secret place, as a wheel, is quickly accomplished.

items.question: Why is the question asked by the great goddess considered difficult even for gods?
premises: The deity expresses strong approval
The great goddess has asked a question
The matter asked about is hard for gods to obtain
items.inference: The goddess has asked about a matter that is well-posed yet difficult even for the gods
items.plain_english: Well said, well said, O great goddess! You have asked me about something hard for even the gods to obtain.

rows.grounds: state assigned to the syllable kṣa

items.question: Which bodily locations correspond to the syllables kṣa and laṃ?
premises: The syllable kṣa is assigned a specific state
That state is identified as brahmarandhra
The syllable laṃ is located in the forehead
items.inference: The syllable kṣa corresponds to the brahmarandhra and the syllable laṃ to the forehead
uncertainties: lalāṭayoḥ is dual in form though often used for the forehead region
items.plain_english: The syllable kṣa is the state of the brahmarandhra, and the syllable laṃ is in the forehead.

rows.grounds: object located in the throat region

items.question: Which bodily locations correspond to the syllables ṣa and śa?
premises: The syllable ṣa is assigned to a bodily region
That region is the throat
The syllable śa is assigned to the heart
items.inference: The syllable ṣa corresponds to the throat region and the syllable śa to the heart
items.plain_english: The syllable ṣa is in the region of the throat, and the syllable śa is then in the heart.

rows.grounds: states that the wheels have been taught

items.question: What instruction follows after the place-wheels have been declared?
premises: The place-wheels have been declared
Their meditation remains to be taught
The listener is invited to hear it
items.inference: After declaring the place-wheels, the teaching turns to their meditation
items.plain_english: Thus the place-wheels have been declared; now hear their meditation, O beloved.

rows.grounds: second member indicating the adorning group

items.question: How is the divine lotus of the first octad to be visualized?
premises: The object of meditation is a lotus
The lotus is divine and eight-spoked
It is adorned by the first octad
items.inference: One should visualize a divine eight-spoked lotus adorned by the first octad
items.plain_english: Visualize a divine eight-spoked lotus adorned by the first octad.

rows.grounds: object to be abandoned; sandhi form with following ca

items.question: What conduct should be abandoned once practice yields mental equanimity?
premises: Practice leads to an even mind
Mental equanimity changes one's orientation
Village duties become obstacles to abandon
items.inference: Through practice, one with an even mind should abandon village duties
uncertainties: grāma-dharmañ may refer broadly to conventional social duties
items.plain_english: Through practice, with an even mind, one should abandon the duties of village life.

items.question: What powers arise from this practice regarding distant hearing and bondage?
premises: The practice yields special knowledge
One power is hearing from afar
Another power is the paralysis of bonds
items.inference: The practice grants knowledge of distant hearing and the power to paralyze bonds
uncertainties: pāśa-stobham may mean arresting or immobilizing bonds
items.plain_english: O beloved, one gains knowledge of hearing from afar and likewise the power to paralyze bonds.

items.question: What further attainments are summarized as resulting from this practice?
premises: Additional results are being stated
Immortality is among these results
Transformation is also attained
items.inference: In brief, the practice yields immortality and transformation
uncertainties: parivartanam may refer to bodily or experiential transformation
items.plain_english: Likewise, O goddess, in brief one attains immortality and transformation.

items.question: How is the second eight-petaled lotus characterized in meditation?
premises: A second lotus is introduced
It has eight petals
It is brightly illuminated through fiery meditation
items.inference: The second eight-petaled lotus is well illuminated by meditation on fire
items.plain_english: The second is an eight-petaled lotus, well illuminated by meditation on fire.

rows.grounds: describes the mind absorbed in meditation

items.question: What ability arises for one whose mind is absorbed in single-pointed meditation?
premises: The mind becomes one-pointed in meditation
Such absorption enables creative power
The practitioner can assume forms in many ways
items.inference: One whose mind is absorbed in single-pointed meditation can create many forms
items.plain_english: One whose mind is absorbed in single-pointed meditation can assume many forms.

rows.grounds: condition under which the power acts
describes the triple world as moving and unmoving

items.question: What destructive power is attributed to the practitioner when angered?
premises: The practitioner may become angry
Anger activates a destructive capacity
The scope includes the entire triple world
items.inference: When angered, the practitioner can destroy the entire triple world, moving and unmoving
items.plain_english: But when angry, he can destroy the entire triple world, with all that moves and does not move.

rows.grounds: second member indicating the nine principles
describes the function of the wheel

items.question: What liberating function is attributed to the third great wheel?
premises: A third great wheel is introduced
The wheel has a specific function
Its function is liberation from the nine principles
items.inference: The third great wheel liberates one from the nine principles
uncertainties: nava-tattva may refer to a specific set of nine principles in this system
items.plain_english: The third is the great wheel, which liberates one from the nine principles.

items.question: What bodily and perceptual powers result from this wheel's practice?
premises: The practice affects bodily aging signs
Wrinkles and grey hair are removed
Perception extends to very distant things
items.inference: The practice brings destruction of wrinkles and grey hair and the ability to see from very far away
items.plain_english: It brings the destruction of wrinkles and grey hair, and likewise the ability to see from very far away.

rows.grounds: object of intent; sandhi form with following ca

items.question: How should a practitioner cultivate multiple forms through solitary meditation?
premises: The practice is to be done in solitude
The practitioner must be intent on meditation
Multiple forms are to be created
items.inference: In solitude, intent on meditation, one should create many forms
items.plain_english: In solitude, intent on meditation, create many forms.

items.question: What result comes to one devoted to constant practice of this discipline?
premises: The practitioner is devoted to constant practice
Continuous effort is emphasized
Immortality is the stated outcome
items.inference: One intent on constant practice indeed attains immortality
items.plain_english: Indeed, one who is intent on constant practice attains immortality.

items.question: How does abstaining from food by day affect death from aging?
premises: A regimen of non-eating by day is practiced
This practice targets age-related death
The outcome is described as going beyond it
items.inference: Through non-eating by day, one will overcome death from aging
uncertainties: divasāt nāśanena may mean fasting during the day or abstaining for days
items.plain_english: Indeed, through abstaining from food by day, one will overcome death from aging.

items.question: What bodily form results from constant yogic practice over time?
premises: The practice is constant yogic discipline
A specific age-form is mentioned
The result is attaining the form of sixteen years
items.inference: Through constant yogic practice, one attains the form of a sixteen-year-old
items.plain_english: Through constant yogic practice, one becomes of the form of a sixteen-year-old.

items.question: What power arises from continually contemplating a smoke-colored form?
premises: The meditation object is smoke-colored
The contemplation is performed continually
The result affects the triple world
items.inference: By continually contemplating a smoke-colored form, one can shake the triple world
items.plain_english: O beloved, by always contemplating a smoke-colored form, one can shake the triple world.
